title: Number of Islands
description:
Given an `m x n` 2D binary `grid` representing a map of `'1'`s (land) and `'0'`s (water), return the total number of **islands**.

An **island** is surrounded by water and is formed by connecting adjacent land cells horizontally or vertically (4-directionally). Diagonal land cells are **not** considered connected. You may assume all four edges of the grid are surrounded by water.
hints: Treat the grid as an undirected graph where each `'1'` cell is a vertex connected to its 4-directional `'1'` neighbors; the answer is the number of connected components.
Scan every cell in the grid. Whenever you encounter an unvisited `'1'`, increment the island count and run BFS or DFS to mark all cells in that island as visited.
To avoid hitting recursion limits on large snake-shaped islands, prefer an iterative BFS queue or an explicit DFS stack.

examples.explanation: All nine land cells are connected horizontally or vertically into a single island.
There is a 2x2 island in the top-left, a single-cell island at (2, 2) (diagonals do not connect), and a 1x2 island in the bottom-right.
In a 3x3 checkerboard of land and water, none of the five `'1'` cells share a horizontal or vertical edge, so each is its own island.
